Attached are Acme's redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see MSA_Acme_Redwood_Redlines_20260214.pdf). A few high-priority points our legal team flagged that we need to resolve before procurement can sign: 

- Limitation of Liability (Section 8): Acme is proposing a cap equal to 12 months of prepaid fees rather than 3 months.
- Consequential Damages: We accept a general exclusion, but we need a carve-out for breaches of confidentiality, data protection obligations, and third-party indemnities.
- Refunds on termination for convenience: For prepaid/committed fees, Acme requests an explicit entitlement to a pro-rata refund for unused portions upon termination for convenience.
- Wind-down Assistance: If Redwood charges for wind-down assistance, Acme wants those fees excluded from any LoL cap so that required support during transition isn't limited by the damages cap.

Given our procurement timeline, can you confirm Redwood's positions on (i) whether refund obligations are treated as damages under the LoL, (ii) whether wind-down assistance can be carved out from the cap, and (iii) whether Redwood can accept the 12-month cap?

Jordan — thanks for the redlines and callout. I reviewed with our legal and pricing teams this morning; high-level positions below so we can get procurement moving: 

1) Liability cap: Our standard is a cap equal to the higher of (i) fees paid in the prior 3 months and (ii) $250,000. For larger committed deals we can discuss moving to a 12-month lookback for the cap, but that typically requires a revenue commitment (Order Form revision) or an uplift to support/SLA pricing.

2) Refunds on termination for convenience (prepaid fees): By default our practice is that prepaid fees are non-refundable; however, we're open to a pro-rata credit for unused term as a commercial accommodation. That accommodation is typically treated as a refund/credit rather than damages — i.e., it reduces future obligations rather than creating a damages exposure.

3) Wind-down assistance: Redwood provides optional wind-down assistance (transition services) as a professional services engagement. We can offer a short window (e.g., 30 days) at a discounted rate as part of the Order Form. Those service fees are usually payable and would be recorded as fees, and we prefer they be subject to the same cap as other contractual payment obligations.

4) Carve-outs: We will accept carve-outs from the exclusion of consequential damages for (a) breaches of confidentiality and data protection commitments and (b) third-party indemnity claims. We will not carve out routine service fees or wind-down assistance as unlimited exposures.

I'll defer to Marissa on precise redline language we can propose. If Acme needs the 12-month cap as a hard legal term rather than a commercial concession, let us know what committed spend Acme proposes so I can run the numbers with finance.

Best,

Sooj — appreciate the quick reply. A few follow-ups from Acme legal: 

> "we're open to a pro-rata credit for unused term as a commercial accommodation. That accommodation is typically treated as a refund/credit rather than damages"

Acme's concern is that if refunds/credits are treated as non-damages, Redwood could still limit its refund obligation via the LoL cap (i.e., treating refunds as a damages offset subject to the cap). We need express contractual language that (1) refunds of prepaid fees due to Customer termination for convenience are not subject to the limitation of liability, or (2) alternatively, that the refund is payable regardless of the cap.

On wind-down assistance: Acme's position is that required transition support (e.g., export of customer data, knowledge transfer, and minimal runbook handover) should not be subject to the LoL cap — the ability to obtain these services post-termination is a core operational need. We're willing to pay for these services, but they should be enforceable and not limited to the damages cap.

Procurement deadline is Feb 23. Could your legal propose explicit wording we can review? If possible, escalate to your legal lead — we need a commitment on the refund carve-out.

Jordan

Sooj / Aditya — following up with proposed compromise language that balances Acme's operational needs and Redwood's risk profile. Below is redline-ready text our counsel recommends. Please review and, if you agree, send to Acme with an offer of a 30-minute legal-to-legal call.

Proposed language (suggested placement: Section 8, Limitation of Liability):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, (a) the aggregate liability of Redwood for damages arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability, or (ii) $500,000; and (b) the foregoing limitation shall not apply to liability arising from (i) Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence, (ii) Redwood's breach of its confidentiality or data protection obligations, or (iii) Redwood's indemnification obligations to third parties.

For the avoidance of doubt, any pro-rata refund of prepaid fees due to Customer's termination for convenience shall be treated as a refund of fees rather than as damages, and shall be payable to Customer; provided, however, that such refund obligation shall not increase Redwood's aggregate liability under Section 8(a) above for damages unrelated to refunds. Wind-down assistance fees (including any transition services specifically identified in the Order Form) shall be treated as fees for services and, except to the extent expressly stated otherwise in the Order Form, shall be subject to the limitation of liability described in Section 8(a)."

Rationale: this preserves Acme's right to a commercially reasonable pro-rata refund on termination for convenience (so refunds are not shoehorned into the damages bucket), while keeping damage exposures (e.g., consequential claims tied to service issues) within a manageable cap. Wind-down assistance is treated as a fee-based professional service so we can price and limit exposure.

If Acme insists that wind-down assistance fees be excluded from the cap, our commercial fallback is to offer a contract amendment that includes a standalone wind-down allowance (pre-funded or insured) or an increased liability cap tied to the Order Form value.

Next steps: if you want to propose the above to Acme, I recommend offering the 30-minute law-to-law call and anchoring commercial options (12-month cap vs. 3-month cap) to a defined committed spend level.
